commands.title: List files with sizes and hidden files
commands.description: Long listing with human-readable sizes, including dotfiles.

commands.title: List newest files first
commands.description: Shows the 20 most recently modified entries in the current folder.

commands.title: Show a directory tree to a depth
commands.description: Prints the folder structure down to two levels; install with apt if tree is missing.

commands.title: Find files by name
commands.description: Searches recursively for files matching a glob such as *.log; quote the pattern.

commands.title: Find files by name, case-insensitive
commands.description: Like find -name but ignores upper/lower case.

commands.title: Find files larger than a size
commands.description: Lists files over 100 MB; use k, M or G for other units.

commands.title: Find files modified in the last day
commands.description: Lists files changed within the last 24 hours.

commands.title: Find files older than N days
commands.description: Lists files not modified for more than 30 days.

commands.title: Find only directories
commands.description: Searches recursively for folders matching a name pattern.

commands.title: Find and delete old files
commands.description: Permanently deletes files older than 30 days; run it without -delete first to preview.

commands.title: Find empty directories
commands.description: Lists folders that contain nothing; add -delete to remove them.

commands.title: Find empty files
commands.description: Lists zero-byte files.

commands.title: Size of each item in a folder, sorted
commands.description: Shows how big every entry here is, smallest to largest.

commands.title: Count files in a directory
commands.description: Counts files recursively, not including folders.

commands.title: Copy a folder recursively
commands.description: Copies a directory with everything inside it; add -a to keep permissions and timestamps.

commands.title: Move or rename a file
commands.description: Moves or renames; silently overwrites an existing destination unless you add -i.

commands.title: Create nested directories
commands.description: Creates the folder and any missing parents without error if it already exists.

commands.title: Create a symbolic link
commands.description: Makes link-name point at target; give the target as an absolute path to avoid broken links.

commands.title: Show file metadata
commands.description: Prints size, permissions, owner, inode and access/modify/change times.

commands.title: Identify a file's type
commands.description: Detects the real type of a file from its contents, not its extension.

commands.title: Count lines in a file
commands.description: Prints the number of lines.

commands.title: Show the first lines of a file
commands.description: Prints the first 20 lines.

commands.title: Show the last lines of a file
commands.description: Prints the last 50 lines.

commands.title: Follow a file as it grows
commands.description: Streams new lines as they are appended, useful for logs; Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.title: Follow a file in less
commands.description: Follows like tail -f but lets you press Ctrl+C to scroll and F to resume.

commands.title: Compare two files in unified format
commands.description: Shows differences as a patch with context lines.

commands.title: Resolve the absolute path of a file
commands.description: Prints the full canonical path, following symlinks.

commands.title: Create an empty file or update its timestamp
commands.description: Creates the file if missing, otherwise sets its modified time to now.

commands.title: Update the file-name index and locate a file
commands.description: Rebuilds the locate database then searches it; much faster than find but only as fresh as the last updatedb.

commands.title: Rename files by pattern
commands.description: Perl rename: replaces the first match in every file name in this folder; add -n to preview.

commands.title: Change a file extension on many files
commands.command: for f in *.<ext>; do mv "$f" "${f%.<ext>}.<newext>"; done
commands.description: Renames every matching file in the current folder to the new extension.

commands.title: Show disk space per filesystem
commands.description: Human-readable usage and free space for every mounted filesystem.

commands.title: Show disk space excluding temp filesystems
commands.description: Adds filesystem type and hides tmpfs and devtmpfs noise.

commands.title: Check inode usage
commands.description: Shows inodes used and free; a full inode table blocks new files even with free space.

commands.title: Find the biggest folders under a path
commands.description: Lists the 15 largest subfolders, biggest first.

commands.title: Browse disk usage interactively
commands.description: Ncurses disk usage browser; install with apt install ncdu. Press d to delete, q to quit.

commands.title: Find the largest files on a path
commands.command: sudo find <dir> -xdev -type f -size +100M -exec ls -lh {} + 2> /dev/null | sort -k5 -rh | head -20
commands.description: Lists files over 100 MB on one filesystem, largest first.

commands.title: Find directories using the most inodes
commands.command: sudo find <dir> -xdev -type f | cut -d/ -f1-3 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
commands.description: Counts files per top-level folder to find where inodes are being used up.

commands.title: List block devices
commands.description: Shows disks, partitions and mount points as a tree.

commands.title: List block devices with filesystems
commands.description: Adds filesystem type, label and UUID for each partition.

commands.title: Show UUIDs and filesystem types
commands.description: Prints the UUID, label and type of each block device, for use in /etc/fstab.

commands.title: List partition tables
commands.description: Shows every disk with its partition layout and sizes.

commands.title: Show mounts as a tree
commands.description: Lists mounted filesystems with source and options.

commands.title: Find which mount holds a path
commands.description: Shows the filesystem that a given file or folder lives on.

commands.title: Mount a partition
commands.description: Mounts the device at an existing empty directory.

commands.title: Unmount a filesystem
commands.description: Unmounts cleanly; fails if the filesystem is busy.

commands.title: Force unmount a busy filesystem
commands.description: Forces the unmount, which can lose unwritten data; try umount -l (lazy) if the mount is hung.

commands.title: See which processes use a mount
commands.description: Lists open files on a mount point, to find what keeps it busy.

commands.title: Watch disk I/O per process
commands.description: Shows only processes doing I/O, with accumulated totals; install with apt install iotop.

commands.title: Show disk I/O statistics
commands.description: Per-device utilisation, throughput and wait times every second; from the sysstat package.

commands.title: Show swap in use
commands.description: Lists swap files and partitions with size and usage.

commands.title: Create and enable a 2 GB swap file
commands.command: sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile && sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile
commands.description: Allocates a swap file and turns it on; add it to /etc/fstab to survive reboots.

commands.title: Disable a swap file
commands.description: Stops using the swap file; fails if there is not enough free RAM to take the contents.

commands.title: Clear the apt package cache
commands.description: Deletes downloaded .deb files from /var/cache/apt/archives to free space.

commands.title: Remove unused packages
commands.description: Removes dependencies nobody needs any more, with their config files.

commands.title: Check a filesystem for errors
commands.description: Read-only check (-n makes no changes); never run a repairing fsck on a mounted filesystem.

commands.title: Show SMART health of a disk
commands.description: Prints drive health and error logs; install with apt install smartmontools.

commands.title: Live process monitor
commands.description: Shows CPU, memory and the busiest processes; press q to quit, M to sort by memory.

commands.title: Friendlier process monitor
commands.description: Interactive viewer with search, tree view and kill; install with apt install htop.

commands.title: Top memory-consuming processes
commands.description: Lists the 10 processes using the most memory.

commands.title: Top CPU-consuming processes
commands.description: Lists the 10 processes using the most CPU.

commands.title: Show the process tree
commands.description: Prints every process with parent and child relationships.

commands.title: Find a process by name
commands.description: Lists PIDs and full command lines of processes whose name matches.

commands.title: Kill processes by name
commands.description: Sends SIGTERM to every process matching the name; check with pgrep -a first.

commands.title: Kill a process by PID
commands.description: Asks the process to terminate gracefully with SIGTERM.

commands.title: Force kill a process
commands.description: Sends SIGKILL, which cannot be caught and skips cleanup; use only when kill fails.

commands.title: Kill all processes with a name
commands.description: Terminates every process with exactly this name.

commands.title: Start a command at low priority
commands.description: Runs the command with a lower CPU priority (higher nice value).

commands.title: Change priority of a running process
commands.description: Raises the nice value of a running process; negative values need root.

commands.title: List files opened by a process
commands.description: Shows open files, sockets and libraries for one PID.

commands.title: Show memory usage
commands.description: Displays total, used, free and cached RAM and swap in human units.

commands.title: Virtual memory and CPU stats every second
commands.description: Prints run queue, swap, I/O and CPU columns once a second; Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.title: Show uptime and load average
commands.description: Shows how long the system has been up and the 1, 5 and 15 minute load averages.

commands.title: Count CPU cores
commands.description: Prints the number of processing units available.

commands.title: Repeat a command every few seconds
commands.description: Reruns the command every 2 seconds and shows the output full screen.

commands.title: Trace the system calls of a process
commands.description: Attaches to a running process and prints its syscalls; slows it down, Ctrl+C to detach.

commands.title: Time how long a command takes
commands.description: Prints real, user and sys time after the command finishes.

commands.title: Run a command that survives logout
commands.description: Starts it in the background immune to hangups, writing output to nohup.out.

commands.title: List background jobs
commands.description: Shows jobs started from this shell and their state.

commands.title: Resume a job in the foreground
commands.description: Brings job number 1 back to the foreground.

commands.title: Resume a job in the background
commands.description: Continues a stopped job (after Ctrl+Z) in the background.

commands.title: Show threads of a process
commands.description: Lists every thread of one process.

commands.title: Show a process's start time and elapsed time
commands.description: Tells you when a process started and how long it has run.

commands.title: Show per-CPU usage
commands.description: Per-core utilisation every second; from the sysstat package.

commands.title: Show IP addresses
commands.description: Brief list of interfaces with state and addresses.

commands.title: Show full interface details
commands.description: Full address information for every network interface.

commands.title: Show the routing table
commands.description: Lists routes including the default gateway.

commands.title: Show the route to a destination
commands.description: Shows which interface and gateway will be used to reach an address.

commands.title: List listening ports with processes
commands.description: Shows TCP and UDP listeners with the owning process and PID.

commands.title: Show socket summary
commands.description: Prints counts of sockets by state and protocol.

commands.title: Show which process listens on a port
commands.description: Lists the processes with that port open, with their PID and user; needs sudo to see other users' processes.

commands.title: Show established connections
commands.description: Lists current TCP connections with addresses and ports.

commands.title: Fetch only the response headers
commands.description: Sends a HEAD request and prints the status line and headers.

commands.title: Verbose request details
commands.description: Shows the TLS handshake, request and response headers for debugging.

commands.title: Follow redirects and show the final URL
commands.description: Follows redirects and prints where you end up.

commands.title: Download a file with curl
commands.description: Saves the response to a file and follows redirects.

commands.title: POST JSON with curl
commands.description: Sends a JSON body in a POST request.

commands.title: Send an authorization header
commands.description: Calls an API with a bearer token; avoid leaving tokens in shell history.

commands.title: Measure download speed with curl
commands.description: Downloads and discards the body, printing the average speed.

commands.title: Time each phase of a request
commands.command: curl -o /dev/null -s -w "dns %{time_namelookup}s connect %{time_connect}s tls %{time_appconnect}s first byte %{time_starttransfer}s total %{time_total}s\n" <url>
commands.description: Breaks down where the time goes for a request.

commands.title: Download a file with wget
commands.description: Saves the file in the current folder.

commands.title: Resume a partial download with wget
commands.description: Continues a download that was interrupted.

commands.title: Mirror a page for offline use
commands.description: Downloads a site section with its assets and rewrites links to work locally.

commands.title: Ping a host four times
commands.description: Sends four ICMP echo requests and prints latency and loss.

commands.title: Trace the route to a host
commands.description: Shows each hop to the destination; install with apt install traceroute.

commands.title: Combined ping and traceroute report
commands.description: Sends 10 probes per hop and prints a report of loss and latency; install with apt install mtr-tiny.

commands.title: Look up DNS records
commands.description: Queries the default resolver and shows the full answer.

commands.title: Short DNS answer
commands.description: Prints only the resolved addresses.

commands.title: Query a specific record type
commands.description: Looks up a record type such as MX, TXT or NS.

commands.title: Query a specific DNS server
commands.description: Asks a chosen resolver instead of the system default.

commands.title: Trace DNS resolution from the root
commands.description: Follows delegation from the root servers to the authoritative answer.

commands.title: Reverse DNS lookup
commands.description: Finds the hostname for an IP address.

commands.title: Look up a name with nslookup
commands.description: Simple DNS lookup showing the server used and the answer.

commands.title: Look up a name with host
commands.description: One-line DNS lookup summary.

commands.title: Test whether a TCP port is open
commands.description: Tries to connect without sending data and reports success or failure.

commands.title: Show my public IP address
commands.description: Asks an external service for the IP address you appear from.

commands.title: Show local IP addresses
commands.description: Prints all non-loopback addresses of this machine.

commands.title: Edit the hosts file
commands.description: Maps names to IP addresses locally, overriding DNS; one entry per line.

commands.title: Show DNS resolver status
commands.description: Shows the DNS servers and domains systemd-resolved uses per interface.

commands.title: Flush the DNS cache
commands.description: Clears systemd-resolved cached answers.

commands.title: Capture packets on a port

commands.title: Save a packet capture to a file
commands.description: Writes raw packets for later analysis in Wireshark.

commands.title: Show interface traffic counters
commands.description: Prints bytes, packets and errors per interface.

commands.title: Show Wi-Fi and network connections
commands.description: Lists network devices and their state in NetworkManager.

commands.title: Connect with a port and key
commands.description: Logs in on a custom port using a specific private key.

commands.title: Connect through a jump host
commands.description: Reaches a host through a bastion in a single command.

commands.title: Generate an ed25519 key pair

commands.title: List keys loaded in the agent
commands.description: Shows fingerprints of keys the agent holds.

commands.title: Remove a stale host key
commands.description: Deletes the host from known_hosts after a server was reinstalled.

commands.title: Forward a local port
commands.description: Makes the remote service reachable at localhost on your machine.

commands.title: Forward a remote port back to you
commands.description: Exposes a local service on the remote server's port.

commands.title: Open a SOCKS proxy through a server
commands.description: Starts a SOCKS5 proxy on localhost routed through the server; -N runs no command.

commands.description: Uploads over SSH; use -P for a non-default port.

commands.title: Copy a file from a server
commands.description: Downloads over SSH into a local folder.

commands.title: Copy a folder to a server
commands.description: Recursively uploads a directory over SSH.

commands.title: Sync a folder with rsync
commands.description: Copies only changed files, compressed, keeping permissions; the trailing slash on the source matters.

commands.title: Mirror a folder, deleting extras
commands.description: Makes the destination identical to the source, deleting files that are not in it; test with --dry-run.

commands.title: Preview an rsync without changing anything
commands.description: Dry run that lists what would be copied or deleted.

commands.title: Open an SFTP session
commands.description: Interactive file transfer shell with get, put, ls and cd.

commands.title: Debug an SSH connection
commands.description: Prints detailed handshake and authentication output to diagnose failures.

commands.title: Run a command on a remote host
commands.description: Executes one command remotely and returns its output.

commands.title: Show a server's host key fingerprint
commands.description: Prints the fingerprint to verify before trusting a new host.

commands.title: Create a tar.gz archive
commands.description: Packs and compresses a folder with gzip.

commands.title: Read a compressed file without extracting
commands.description: Prints the uncompressed content to the terminal.

commands.title: Search inside compressed logs

commands.title: Create a 7z archive
commands.description: High-compression archive; install with apt install p7zip-full.

commands.title: Extract a 7z archive
commands.description: Extracts with the full folder structure.

commands.title: Search files recursively for text

commands.title: Search case-insensitively
commands.description: Ignores letter case when matching.

commands.title: Show lines that do not match
commands.description: Inverts the match, printing only non-matching lines.

commands.title: Count matching lines

commands.title: Match with an extended regex
commands.description: Matches either alternative using extended regular expressions.

commands.title: Print one column with awk

commands.title: Compute a SHA-256 checksum

commands.title: Count words, lines and bytes

commands.title: Show unique values of a column
